decisive_reason: RIGHT presents the stronger end-to-end artifact proof: a completed runner-only Cortex Code execution, persisted Snowpark policy output, query and session provenance, 47 passing tests, and a public Streamlit product that reloads the authenticated run. LEFT describes a broad and relevant Snowflake architecture, but its supplied proof is weighted more toward repository assets and reproducibility instructions, while the Snowflake dashboard itself is not publicly inspectable and the public MVP is a separate Mendix application.

LEFT: No signed-out access to the Snowflake dashboard.
The packet does not show an independently observed successful full-pipeline execution or production outcome.
The public MVP is separate from the Snowflake Streamlit surface, leaving the deployed end-to-end integration less directly demonstrated.
RIGHT: No outcome from an open live tender submission.

confidence.rationale: The supplied cards differ clearly in execution evidence and product closure. Confidence is limited to the frozen packet because no external verification or identity inference was permitted.
